name: WinCo Foods
desc: Employee-owned discount supermarket chain selling groceries, bakery, produce, bulk foods and general merchandise in the western US.
markets: Supermarkets across the western United States, including Idaho, Utah and Southern Nevada.
rationale: Large western-US grocer; F1's Las Vegas race and growing US audience offer regional hospitality and staff-reward platforms.

name: Stater Bros. Markets
desc: Privately held supermarket chain operating 171 stores in Southern California, mainly in San Bernardino and Riverside counties.
markets: 171 supermarkets throughout Southern California, primarily the Inland Empire.
rationale: Southern California grocer; F1's growing US fan base could support consumer promotions, though the business is purely regional.

name: Schnucks
desc: Family-owned supermarket chain founded in 1939, operating stores across Missouri, Illinois, Indiana and, since 2025, Wisconsin.
markets: 113 stores in Missouri, Illinois and Indiana, plus 51 Wisconsin stores bought in October 2025.
rationale: Expanding Midwest grocer; F1 content could freshen loyalty marketing, but the regional footprint limits global sponsorship value.

name: Save Mart Supermarkets
desc: Supermarket operator running Save Mart, Lucky and FoodMaxx stores in northern and central California and northern Nevada.
capacity_detail: Revenue US$4.6bn (2019); also co-title sponsor of NASCAR Cup Toyota/Save Mart 350 (2026)
sponsorships: NASCAR Cup Series: Toyota/Save Mart 350 at Sonoma (2026, co-title)
markets: 194 stores under Save Mart, Lucky and FoodMaxx in northern and central California and northern Nevada.
rationale: Already a NASCAR Cup race title partner, so motorsport sponsorship is proven; F1 could extend that with US-race activations.

name: Market Basket
desc: Demoulas family-owned supermarket chain operating about 90 stores in Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Maine and Rhode Island.
markets: About 90 supermarkets in Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Maine and Rhode Island.
rationale: High-revenue New England grocer; limited reach makes F1 a long shot beyond hospitality or supplier entertainment.

name: Total Wine & More
desc: Private retailer of wine, spirits, beer and cigars with 259 superstores in 28 US states and online sales.
markets: 259 stores in 28 US states, with online sales in 24 states (October 2023).
rationale: Largest US drinks retailer; F1 is rich in spirits and champagne partners, enabling co-promotions with supplier brands.

name: Rural King
desc: Farm supply retail chain selling automotive, outdoor, pet, hardware and farm products across eastern and southern US states.
markets: 135 stores in states including Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, Kentucky, Tennessee, Florida, Michigan and Alabama (2024).
rationale: Rural retailer whose customers lean to NASCAR; F1 fit is weak beyond US-race promotions.

name: Fleet Farm
desc: Retail chain selling farm supplies, hunting and fishing gear, hardware, automotive and household goods in the upper Midwest.
markets: 50 stores in Minnesota, Iowa, Wisconsin, North Dakota and South Dakota.
rationale: PE-owned Midwest retailer; F1 sponsorship unlikely apart from small US-market promotions around automotive categories.

name: Ace Hardware
desc: Retailer-owned hardware cooperative supplying more than 5,200 independently owned Ace stores in 60 countries.
markets: Over 5,200 locations in 60 countries; distribution centres in the US, China, Panama and the UAE.
rationale: Global hardware brand with dealer network; F1 hospitality and tool-themed content could rival DeWalt and Haas tie-ins.

name: Do it Best
desc: Member-owned hardware, lumber and building materials cooperative that bought True Value out of bankruptcy in 2024.
markets: Member-owned stores across the United States and more than 50 other countries, plus True Value and Hardware Hank brands.
rationale: Enlarged after True Value deal; motorsport hospitality could reward member retailers, though budgets are cooperative and cautious.

name: Rooms To Go
desc: Private furniture retailer selling furniture, mattresses, bedding, home decor and rugs through showrooms and online.
markets: Furniture showrooms in the United States, headquartered near Tampa, Florida.
rationale: Florida-based furniture chain; F1's Miami Grand Prix offers a home-region consumer-marketing and hospitality platform.

name: Staples
desc: Office supplies, furniture and technology retailer operating 827 US stores plus business delivery services.
markets: 827 stores in the United States (2026) plus B2B delivery through Quill and HiTouch Business Services.
rationale: B2B office supplier; F1 hospitality could court corporate buyers, though PE ownership keeps marketing budgets tight.

name: L.L.Bean
desc: Private outdoor clothing, footwear and equipment retailer selling through catalogues, online and stores in the US, Japan and Canada.
markets: 60 US stores in 19 states, 22 stores in Japan, 13 in Canada and about 200 partner stores.
rationale: Heritage outdoor brand strong in Japan; F1's Suzuka and US races fit its two biggest markets.

name: Micro Center
desc: Computer and consumer electronics superstore chain owned by privately held Micro Electronics, Inc.
markets: 30 stores in 20 US states (May 2025).
rationale: PC-builder retailer; esports and F1 sim-racing audiences overlap with its gaming hardware customers.

name: Bi-Mart
desc: Employee-owned members-only discount chain selling electronics, housewares, hardware, sporting goods and food in the Pacific Northwest.
markets: Members-only discount stores in Oregon, Washington and Idaho in the Pacific Northwest.
rationale: Regional membership retailer; F1 sponsorship is unlikely beyond small consumer promotions tied to US race broadcasts.

name: Fareway
desc: Beckwith family-owned grocery chain with meat markets and wholesale operations, founded in Boone, Iowa.
markets: Grocery stores and meat markets founded in Iowa, with wholesale, online meat and catering subsidiaries.
rationale: Regional grocer with limited fit; F1 relevance is low beyond US broadcast-led promotions.

name: Harps Food Stores
desc: Employee-owned regional supermarket chain operating 151 stores across Arkansas, Oklahoma, Missouri, Kansas, Mississippi and Louisiana.
markets: 151 supermarkets in Arkansas, Oklahoma, Missouri, Kansas, Mississippi and Louisiana, entering Tennessee and Kentucky in 2026.
rationale: Expanding southern grocer; F1 relevance is low but US-race hospitality could reward suppliers.

name: Price Chopper Supermarkets
desc: Supermarket chain operating 128 Price Chopper and Market 32 stores in six northeastern states, owned by Northeast Grocery.
markets: 128 stores in upstate New York, Vermont, Connecticut, Massachusetts, New Hampshire and Pennsylvania.
rationale: Regional grocer; F1 fit is weak, limited to supplier hospitality or broadcast-linked promotions.

name: Hallmark Cards
desc: Family-owned greeting card, gift and media group whose businesses include Crayola, Hallmark Channel and Gold Crown stores.
markets: Greeting cards, gifts and media; 1,146 stores (2025); units include Crayola, Hallmark Channel and DaySpring.
rationale: Household brand with media arm; F1's family audience growth could suit Crayola or Hallmark Media content partnerships.

name: In-N-Out Burger
desc: Privately owned burger restaurant chain founded in California and controlled by owner Lynsi Snyder.
markets: Company-operated burger restaurants in the United States, grown from its Southern California base.
rationale: Cult US brand with car-culture heritage; F1's Las Vegas race and US growth offer authentic lifestyle crossover.

name: Whataburger
desc: Texas-based burger chain with more than 820 restaurants in Texas and southern US states, majority-owned by BDT & MSD.
markets: 670+ restaurants in Texas and 150+ in New Mexico, Arizona, Colorado and the South (2019).
rationale: Texas icon; Austin's US Grand Prix sits in its home market, suiting hospitality and fan activations.

name: Raising Cane's Chicken Fingers
desc: Private fast-food chain serving chicken fingers, fries, coleslaw and Texas toast from more than 900 restaurants.
markets: 900+ restaurants (2025) across the United States, with international units since 2014 starting in Kuwait.
rationale: Fast-growing, marketing-heavy brand expanding abroad; F1 races in the US and Middle East match its footprint.

name: Culver's
desc: Family-owned fast-food franchise known for ButterBurgers and frozen custard, with about 1,000 restaurants in 27 states.
markets: About 1,000 restaurants (April 2025) in 27 US states, mainly in the Midwest.
rationale: Midwest restaurant brand; F1 relevance is limited to promotions linked to US race broadcasts and streaming.

name: Golden Corral
desc: Buffet and grill restaurant chain with nearly 500 company-owned and franchised restaurants in 43 US states.
markets: Nearly 500 restaurants in 43 US states, about 100 company-owned.
rationale: Family-dining chain with a broad US base; F1 fit is weak beyond broadcast-led promotions.

name: Waffle House
desc: Restaurant chain serving Southern breakfast food, with more than 2,000 locations in 25 US states.
markets: Over 2,000 restaurants in 25 US states, mainly the South and Midwest.
rationale: Cultural icon in the US South; F1 Miami and Austin races could suit novelty fan activations.

name: Panera Bread
desc: Fast-casual bakery-cafe chain with more than 2,000 locations in the United States and Canada, owned by JAB Holding.
markets: Over 2,000 bakery-cafes in the United States and Canada.
rationale: Large North American restaurant brand; F1's US and Canadian races provide a two-market fan platform.

name: CKE Restaurants
desc: Fast-food company owning Carl's Jr., Hardee's, Green Burrito and Red Burrito, with franchises in 43 foreign countries.
markets: Locations in 44 US states and 43 foreign countries and US territories (October 2020).
rationale: Carl's Jr. has an international franchise base and a bold marketing history suited to F1 audiences.

name: Hooters
desc: Casual dining chain serving wings, burgers and seafood, with franchised restaurants across the US and abroad.
markets: Locations in 44 US states and 28 other countries (2012); over 430 restaurants operated or franchised.
rationale: Franchise network spans the US and 28 countries; F1 fan zones could fit, though its brand image limits partner appeal.

name: TGI Fridays
desc: American casual dining chain with more than 380 restaurants in over 35 countries; filed for US bankruptcy.
markets: More than 380 locations in over 35 countries, including 69 in the United States.
rationale: Global franchise footprint matches F1's calendar, but financial restructuring makes a sponsorship spend unlikely now.

name: White Castle
desc: Ingram family-owned hamburger chain with about 345 restaurants in 13 states and frozen retail sliders.
markets: About 345 restaurants across 13 US states, strongest in the Midwest and New York area.
rationale: Heritage US burger brand; F1 relevance is low beyond novelty promotions around US races.

name: Cook Out
desc: Privately owned drive-thru burger and barbecue chain based in North Carolina, operating in ten US states.
capacity_detail: Title sponsor of NASCAR Cup races Cook Out Clash, Cook Out 400 (Martinsville, Richmond) and Cook Out Southern 500 in 2026
sponsorships: NASCAR Cup Series: Cook Out Clash, Cook Out 400 (Martinsville and Richmond), Cook Out Southern 500 (2026)
markets: Drive-thru restaurants in ten US states, centred on North Carolina and the South.
rationale: Heavy NASCAR title sponsor already buying motorsport; F1's US races could extend that to a younger audience.

name: Arizona Beverage Company
desc: Private maker of AriZona ready-to-drink iced teas, juices, coffees and snacks, sold in all 50 states.
markets: AriZona teas, juices and coffees sold in all 50 US states since 1994.
rationale: Youth-skewed drinks brand facing energy-drink rivals already in F1; trackside sampling could suit its value positioning.

name: Goya Foods
desc: Family-owned producer and distributor of Hispanic foods and beverages sold in the US and many Spanish-speaking countries.
markets: US and Spanish-speaking countries; facilities in the US, Puerto Rico, Dominican Republic and Spain.
rationale: Hispanic-market leader; F1's Mexico City, Miami and Spanish races match its core consumer base.

name: Sargento
desc: Family-owned cheese company producing and marketing packaged sliced, shredded and snack cheese products.
markets: Packaged cheese and food products made in Wisconsin and marketed across the United States.
rationale: Strong US retail brand; F1's US audience growth could support snacking promotions, but fit is modest.

name: Blue Bell Creameries
desc: Private Texas ice cream maker producing packaged ice cream that is sold through retail grocery stores.
markets: Packaged ice cream made in Brenham, Texas, and sold through retail grocery stores.
rationale: Texas brand; the Austin US Grand Prix offers a home-market activation, but national budgets are small.

name: McKee Foods
desc: Family-run bakery making Little Debbie snack cakes plus Drake's Cakes, Fieldstone Bakery and Sunbelt Bakery products.
markets: Little Debbie and other snack brands sold through US grocery and convenience retail.
rationale: Little Debbie is a mass-market US snack brand; F1 fit is low, but US races could support consumer promotions.

name: Taylor Farms
desc: Private producer of fresh-cut salads and vegetables such as lettuce, broccoli and cauliflower for retail and food service.
markets: Fresh vegetables and salads distributed across the United States; past product recalls covered up to 39 states.
rationale: Large B2B fresh-food supplier; F1 hospitality could entertain retail and restaurant buyers, though brand fit is weak.

name: Schreiber Foods
desc: Employee-owned dairy company making natural and processed cheese, cream cheese, yogurt and beverages for customer brands.
markets: US plants plus 12 international facilities in 10 countries including Germany, Brazil, India, Mexico and Spain.
rationale: Global B2B dairy supplier; F1 hospitality could serve customer relationship goals across its international markets.

name: Leprino Foods
desc: Private cheese and dairy-ingredients maker, the largest US exporter of lactose, selling one billion pounds of cheese yearly.
capacity_detail: Sells one billion pounds of cheese per year for US$3bn
markets: Cheese and dairy ingredients for food makers; the largest US exporter of lactose.
rationale: B2B dairy supplier; F1 hospitality could suit key-account entertainment, but consumer brand fit is weak.

name: Ocean Spray
desc: Agricultural cooperative of more than 700 cranberry growers producing juices, sauces and dried fruit.
markets: Member growers in the US, Canada and Chile; juices, sauces and fruit snacks; 70% of North American cranberry output.
rationale: Health-led drinks brand with international reach; F1 hydration and wellness themes could support co-marketing.

name: Jack Link's
desc: Private maker of Jack Link's beef jerky and protein snacks, known for its Messin' with Sasquatch advertising.
capacity_detail: Title sponsor of NASCAR Cup Series Jack Link's 500 at Talladega (2026)
sponsorships: NASCAR Cup Series: Jack Link's 500 at Talladega (2026); Seattle Mariners (2013)
markets: Beef jerky and protein snacks marketed nationally in the United States under the Jack Link's brand.
rationale: Active motorsport and MLB sponsor with protein-snack positioning; F1's fitness and fan audience is a natural next step.

name: Carhartt
desc: Private American workwear brand making durable jackets, overalls and apparel, with some production outsourced to China and Mexico.
markets: Workwear sold in the United States, with production in the US and outsourced to China and Mexico.
rationale: Rugged workwear brand popular with mechanics; F1 pit-crew and garage storytelling suits its 'built tough' positioning.

name: J.Crew
desc: Clothing, shoe and accessories retailer selling through US stores, online and international locations including Japan.
ownership: private: Anchorage Capital Group and Leonard Green & Partners
markets: US stores plus operations in Canada, France, the UK, Hong Kong and 76 locations in Japan.
rationale: Preppy lifestyle brand; F1's fashion-forward paddock and US fan growth suit capsule collaborations, as rival apparel brands show.

name: Bissell
desc: Family-owned maker of vacuum cleaners and floor care products, the North American market leader by sales.
markets: Number one floor-care maker in North America by sales (20% share); brands include Rug Doctor and Sanitaire.
rationale: Household appliance brand; F1 cleanliness and technology content could support marketing against rivals such as SharkNinja, already in F1.

name: Trek Bicycle
desc: Private bicycle and components maker selling through bike shops worldwide, with subsidiaries across Europe and Asia.
markets: Bike shops across North America plus subsidiaries in Germany, the UK, Netherlands, Spain, Switzerland, Austria, Denmark, Japan, Korea and India.
rationale: Performance bike brand like F1 partner Specialized; shared engineering and speed story could appeal to F1 audiences.

name: John Paul Mitchell Systems
desc: Private professional hair care company behind Paul Mitchell products and a network of Paul Mitchell beauty schools.
markets: Salon hair care products and about 100 Paul Mitchell Schools in the United States.
rationale: Salon brand with lifestyle marketing; F1's growing female and younger fans could suit grooming activations.

name: Hendrick Automotive Group
desc: Largest privately held US automotive retailer, operating 103 dealerships across 13 states and linked to Hendrick Motorsports.
sponsorships: NASCAR Cup Series: HendrickCars.com on Hendrick Motorsports cars (extension through 2026)
markets: 103 dealership locations, 141 franchises and 31 nameplates in 13 states from the Carolinas to California.
rationale: Motorsport-native dealer group selling premium brands; F1 hospitality could reach affluent buyers of the manufacturers it retails.

name: Speedway Motorsports
desc: Owner and operator of 11 US racing circuits, including Charlotte Motor Speedway, controlled by the Smith family.
markets: 11 racing facilities across the United States, headquartered at Charlotte Motor Speedway.
rationale: Track owner seeking new events and partners; an F1 tie-up could support circuit marketing, though it is a rights seller.

name: Confie
desc: Private insurance distributor selling personal and commercial cover through Freeway Insurance, Acceptance and other agency brands.
capacity_detail: Freeway Insurance is title sponsor of the NASCAR Cup Freeway Insurance 500 at Phoenix (2026) and a NASCAR premier partner
sponsorships: NASCAR Cup Series: Freeway Insurance 500 (2026); NASCAR premier partner (from Oct 2025)
markets: Retail agencies, franchises and MGAs across at least 26 US states.
rationale: Already a NASCAR premier partner targeting Hispanic drivers; F1's Mexico City and US races fit that audience.

name: Sentry Insurance
desc: Private insurer offering business, auto and life insurance and financial products from Wisconsin.
markets: Insurance and financial products sold across the United States.
rationale: Business and auto insurer; F1 hospitality could entertain commercial clients and agents, though brand reach is domestic.

name: Auto-Owners Insurance
desc: Mutual insurer selling life, home, car and business insurance through independent agents in 26 states.
markets: Life, home, car and business insurance in 26 US states through independent agents.
rationale: Car-insurance specialist with motorsport-adjacent customers; F1 US races could support agent incentives and brand awareness.

name: Country Financial
desc: Group of insurance and financial services companies offering auto, home, life, farm and commercial insurance in 19 states.
markets: Auto, home, life, farm and commercial insurance plus retirement services for customers in 19 US states.
rationale: Regional insurer; F1 fit is modest, though US race hospitality could reward agents.

name: Penn Mutual
desc: Mutual life insurance and annuities company based in Horsham, Pennsylvania, serving policyholders nationwide.
markets: Life insurance and annuities sold across the United States.
rationale: Wealth-focused life insurer; F1 hospitality could court high-net-worth advisers and their clients.

name: Western & Southern Financial Group
industry: life insurance and financial services group
desc: Mutual financial group offering life insurance, annuities, mutual funds and investment management, including Gerber Life.
markets: Insurance, annuities and asset management across the United States through subsidiaries including Gerber Life and Fort Washington.
rationale: Wealth and annuity distributor; premium F1 hospitality could support adviser and high-net-worth client relationships.

name: Westfield Insurance
desc: Multi-line property and casualty insurer covering personal, commercial, agribusiness and surety lines through agents.
markets: Personal and commercial insurance sold through independent agents in the United States.
rationale: Regional insurer; F1 relevance is low beyond hospitality and incentives for independent agents.

name: Grange Insurance
desc: Mutual insurer offering home, auto and business insurance through more than 4,000 independent agents in 13 states.
markets: 13 US states including Ohio, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Tennessee and Wisconsin.
rationale: Agent-led regional insurer; F1 fit is modest, limited to agent incentives at US races.

name: OneAmerica Financial
desc: Mutual holding group offering life, disability and long-term care insurance, annuities and employee benefits.
markets: Insurance, retirement and employee benefits across the United States.
rationale: Indianapolis-based insurer near IndyCar's home; F1 hospitality could serve employer clients, though fit is modest.

name: Highmark Health
desc: Non-profit health insurer and delivery network operating Highmark Blue Cross Blue Shield plans in several states.
capacity_detail: Revenue US$18.2bn (2016); also naming partner of the NFL Buffalo Bills' Highmark Stadium
sponsorships: NFL: naming rights, Highmark Stadium (Buffalo Bills, 10-year deal from 2021, new stadium from 2026)
markets: Health insurance in Pennsylvania, West Virginia, Delaware and western New York, plus hospitals.
rationale: Already pays for NFL stadium naming; F1 wellness and performance themes could extend its health brand.

name: Blue Shield of California
desc: Mutual benefit health plan serving 4.5 million members and over 65,000 physicians in California.
markets: 4.5 million health plan members in California (2021).
rationale: Large California health plan; F1 relevance is low beyond hospitality for employer clients.

name: CareFirst BlueCross BlueShield
desc: Non-profit Blue Cross Blue Shield licensee insuring 3.5 million people in Maryland and the Washington area.
markets: 3.5 million members in Maryland and the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area.
rationale: Regional health insurer around Washington, D.C.; F1 sponsorship fit is weak beyond employer hospitality.

name: Kaiser Permanente
desc: Integrated health system combining health plans, hospitals and medical groups, serving 13.1 million members.
markets: 13.1 million members (2025) across several US states, with 243,795 employees.
rationale: Huge health system; F1 performance-medicine stories could serve brand marketing, but a domestic, member-based model limits fit.

name: AdventHealth
desc: Non-profit hospital network operating healthcare facilities across multiple US states, headquartered in Florida.
capacity_detail: Revenue US$8.31bn (2024); also title sponsor of NASCAR Cup AdventHealth 400 (2026)
sponsorships: NASCAR Cup Series: AdventHealth 400 at Kansas (2026)
markets: Hospitals and healthcare facilities across multiple US states, centred on Florida.
rationale: Already a NASCAR race title sponsor; F1's Miami Grand Prix sits in its Florida heartland.

name: Hensel Phelps
desc: Employee-owned construction, development and facilities management firm based in Colorado.
markets: Construction and facilities projects across the United States.
rationale: Large builder; F1 hospitality could court public and private clients, though consumer brand fit is weak.

name: DPR Construction
desc: Private general contractor and construction management company based in Redwood City, California, building across the United States.
markets: Building and construction management projects across the United States from Redwood City, California.
rationale: Large contractor; technology-themed F1 hospitality could reach corporate clients, though consumer brand fit is weak.

name: Suffolk Construction
desc: Private construction company providing building and construction management services, headquartered in Boston.
markets: Building and construction management projects in the United States, headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts.
rationale: Major Boston builder; F1 hospitality could court developers and institutional clients, though consumer fit is weak.

name: Brasfield & Gorrie
desc: Privately held general contractor headquartered in Birmingham, Alabama, with revenue above US$6bn in 2024.
markets: Construction projects in the United States from its Birmingham, Alabama headquarters.
rationale: Regional builder; F1 relevance is low beyond hospitality for healthcare and commercial clients.

name: Rosendin
desc: Employee-owned electrical contractor, one of the largest in the US, with over 12,000 employees.
markets: Offices in Arizona, California, Hawaii, Maryland, Idaho, North Carolina, Nevada and other states.
rationale: Electrical contractor for data centres and renewables; F1 hospitality could court technology clients.

name: Barton Malow
desc: Private construction services company based in Michigan, with the LIFTbuild subsidiary.
markets: Construction services projects in the United States, headquartered in Southfield, Michigan, with LIFTbuild subsidiary.
rationale: Michigan builder; F1 relevance is low beyond client hospitality for large project owners.

name: Epic Systems
desc: Privately held developer of large-scale electronic health records software for hospitals and health systems.
markets: Health systems in the US and Europe, including the UK, Denmark, Finland and Norway.
rationale: Fast-growing software firm entering Europe; F1 B2B hospitality could support health-system sales, though marketing is restrained.

name: RSM US
desc: Middle-market audit, tax and consulting partnership, member of the RSM International network spanning 120 countries.
markets: US practice with integrated teams in India and El Salvador; part of a 120-country network.
rationale: Professional-services peers Deloitte and PwC are F1 partners; RSM could target middle-market clients the same way.

name: Epicor
desc: Business software company providing ERP, CRM, supply chain and HCM software to manufacturers, distributors and retailers.
markets: ERP, CRM, supply chain and HCM software for manufacturing, distribution, retail and services businesses.
rationale: Enterprise software rivals such as SAP and IFS sponsor F1; Epicor could use F1 to reach manufacturers.

name: Advance Publications
desc: Newhouse family media company owning Condé Nast, American City Business Journals and stakes in Reddit and Charter.
markets: Condé Nast, American City Business Journals, Advance Local and Turnitin; stakes in Charter Communications and Reddit.
rationale: Condé Nast titles such as GQ and Vogue could co-create F1 lifestyle content and events.

name: Interstate Batteries
desc: Privately owned marketer and distributor of automotive, marine, motorcycle and other batteries through a dealer network.
sponsorships: NASCAR: title sponsor of Joe Gibbs Racing's Cup team from 1992 (historic)
markets: Over 200,000 dealers across all 50 US states and Canada, plus distributors in Central America and the Caribbean.
rationale: Motorsport-native brand with decades of NASCAR sponsorship; F1's US growth offers a bigger stage for its battery story.

name: Young Living
desc: Private multi-level marketing company selling essential oils and home wellness products through distributors.
capacity_detail: Annual sales of more than US$1bn reported 2015 to 2017
markets: Essential oils and wellness products sold through member distributors in the US and abroad.
rationale: Wellness brand reliant on distributor incentives; F1 hospitality could motivate top sellers, though MLM reputation limits fit.

name: doTERRA
desc: Private multi-level marketing company selling essential oils, skin care and nutrition products through Wellness Advocates.
capacity_detail: Company claimed more than US$1bn in sales by end of 2015
markets: Over 3 million Wellness Advocates across 100 countries.
rationale: Global distributor network could be motivated by F1 hospitality, but MLM scrutiny makes a major sponsorship unlikely.

name: Perry Ellis International
desc: Privately held clothing and fashion company owning a portfolio of sportswear and casual brands sold worldwide.
markets: Brands distributed through multiple channels worldwide, headquartered near Miami.
rationale: Miami-based apparel group; F1's Miami Grand Prix offers a home-market showcase for its golf and sportswear lines.

name: Big 5 Sporting Goods
desc: Sporting goods retailer with 410 stores in the western United States, now owned by Worldwide Sports Group Holdings.
ownership: private: Worldwide Sports Group Holdings LLC and Capitol Hill Group
markets: 410 sporting goods stores across the western United States, headquartered in El Segundo, California.
rationale: Recently taken private sporting goods chain; F1 relevance is low beyond US-race promotions.
